1,200 repositories.

When we launched Patchwork CI, we promised it would always be free for open source. Some people told us we were crazy. How would we make money, they asked.

Today we run on 1,200 repositories, and about 900 of them are open source.

One number from those repos stuck with me: 1 in 7 CI failures turned out to be a flaky test. That's a lot of developer hours spent staring at red builds that were never real failures.

Open source gave us more than users. It gave us data, feedback, and a community. Our most-requested feature, GitLab support, came straight from OSS maintainers, and we shipped it on November 12.

Making it free for open source isn't charity. It's why we have a product worth paying for.

We built an app nobody used.

When we launched Rotaship, our mobile app looked good and we were proud of it. We assumed restaurant staff would use it.

Only 12% of staff opened it in the first month.

That's when it clicked. We weren't solving the real problem. We were adding another one.

Restaurant teams don't want another app. They already work in WhatsApp.

So in 2025 we moved everything into WhatsApp.

Since then: 140 outlets, and the median reply time to shift messages is under 20 minutes.

If your users won't come to your product, go to where they already are.

The hardest part was admitting the app we liked wasn't the product they needed.

#ProductManagement #Indonesia #StartupLessons #UserExperience

Losing our first big customer was the best thing that happened to Ledgerline.

We were 5 months in when they left. It hurt.

They had heavily customized their NetSuite instance, and we only supported standard fields. We couldn't serve them as they were, so they found someone who could.

We spent 6 weeks adding support for custom fields. That work changed how we think about customers: we build for how they actually use their systems, not how we assume they do.

Today we serve 38 customers. 11 of them rely on custom fields.

If a customer leaves and tells you why, that's the most useful information you'll get. Listen to it.

What loss shaped your company?

#Startups #SaaS #Leadership #CustomerSuccess #Growth

After 11 years in a clinic, I quit. Here's why.

I always loved being a vet. But something kept breaking my heart.

Day after day, I saw anxious pets so terrified that we had to sedate them just to examine them.

I knew there had to be a better way.

So in 2023, I took the leap and founded Doorstep Vet.

The idea was simple: bring compassionate, high-quality care to pets in the one place they feel safest, their own home.

Today, our team of 4 vets does around 30 home visits a week. And every single one reminds me why we do this.

Calmer pets. Happier owners. Better medicine.

Sometimes the bravest thing you can do is follow your heart.

#Veterinary #PetCare #Melbourne #Entrepreneurship #FollowYourPassion

We raised our prices by 50%. Here's what happened.

In September, we raised Tabwise's price from $8 to $12 per user per month. It was a scary call.

Support costs per customer had doubled since launch. We could cut quality or charge more. We picked charging more.

Hardware is hard. Here's our story.

Our first production run at Shelfwise didn't go as planned. 400 labels shipped with a faulty battery contact.

As a young hardware startup, it would have been easy to cut corners. But that's not who we are.

We decided to recall and replace every one of those 400 labels, at our own cost. It set us back about $7,000. Painful? Absolutely. Worth it? 100%.

Because trust is everything.

We didn't stop there. We introduced a 100% contact test at the factory. Since then, we've had zero contact failures across 6,000 labels.

Mistakes don't define you. How you respond to them does.

To all the hardware founders out there: own your mistakes, fix them fast, and build systems so they never happen again.

#Hardware #Startups #Manufacturing #Leadership #Integrity
